theater: 腓尼基海岸與奧龍特斯河下游

battle.name: 第一次敘利亞戰爭
battle.theater: 腓尼基海岸與奧龍特斯河下游
battle.brief: 前二七四年，托勒密二世以填海築堤、七月圍城攻下腓尼基提爾，再取西頓，兵鋒直指奧龍特斯河谷；安條克一世以方陣與象騎收復內陸，兩國前二七一年議和，腓尼基海岸留在埃及手中。卡面的亞述長矛並非戰場實物，它早於本役六百年退入地下，卻標示出矛兵居中、弓兵居兩翼的近東老譜。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 第一次敘利亞戰爭是前二七四年到前二七一年間，托勒密王朝的埃及王國與塞琉古王國為爭奪基列敘利亞與腓尼基海岸而打的一場有限王國戰爭，也是兩朝此後四個半世紀裡五次敘利亞戰爭的開端。交戰的兩方各自是一個以王權直接控制軍隊的君主國。埃及一方以亞歷山大為都，托勒密二世自前二八五年起以共治者身分坐鎮，國家的組織方式是把馬其頓與希臘的重裝方陣兵、埃及本籍的步兵與弓手、克里特與色雷斯的傭兵混編成軍團，國王自領中軍與預備隊，亞歷山大港的船塢按年批次下水艦隊，負責護送攻城部隊、封鎖敵國港口，並把尼羅河出來的穀物運上前線；托勒密王朝還養著數量可觀的非洲象，用在攻城中撞開城門與嚇退守軍。塞琉古一方以安條克（安提阿基斯）為都，國王安條克一世是塞琉古一世之子，自前二八一年起在位；這個王國的兵源與稅收掛在一批城市的歲入上，軍隊標準是馬其頓方陣在亞洲化之後的樣子：密集的薩里沙長矛手配小圓盾，兩翼由色雷斯式標槍騎兵與重裝騎兵護衛，攻城靠扭力弩砲、投石機、攻城塔與撞錘。塞琉古的後方極深，安納托利亞的皇家大道與兩河的水路可以把兵員、攻城器材與糧秣一直送到奧龍特斯河下游，這是它在持久戰裡最大的優勢。第三方力量同樣要寫清楚：高盧人自前二七九年起大批東進，前二七五年被安條克擊敗於安納托利亞，這場高盧戰爭一度把塞琉古的軍力釘在亞洲西部，卻也讓國王在需要時能抽出精兵南下；另外是腓尼基沿岸的城邦與其僭主，提爾與西頓的統治者各據一方，他們既是托勒密在敘利亞的代理人，也是塞琉古的內應；還有安納托利亞與小亞細亞的流亡貴族與傭兵首領，兩方都在爭取他們。整場戰爭沒有動員全國民眾，兩國也都沒有滅國的目標，爭的是港口、關稅與一條守得住的邊界。
countriesEn: The First Syrian War was a limited dynastic war fought between the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt and the Seleucid Kingdom for the possession of Coele-Syria and the Phoenician coast, from 274 to 271 BC. It was the opening of the five Syrian Wars that the two houses would fight over the following four and a half centuries. Each side was a monarchy in which the king held the army directly in his own hand. On the Egyptian side the capital was Alexandria: Ptolemy II had ruled as co-regent since 285 BC, and the state organised its forces by mixing Macedonian and Greek phalanx infantry with native Egyptian foot and archers and with Cretan, Thracian and Carian mercenaries into a single army, while the king kept the centre and the reserve in his own hand; the shipyards of Alexandria launched fleets batch by batch each year to convoy siege trains, blockade enemy ports and carry grain from the Nile up to the front; the Ptolemies also maintained a substantial herd of African elephants, used to batter gates and to terrify the defenders on the walls. On the Seleucid side the capital was Antioch on the Orontes, and the king was Antiochus I Soter, son of Seleucus I, on the throne from 281 BC. This kingdom drew its soldiers and its revenue from the income of its cities, and its army was the Macedonian phalanx in its Asian form: dense sarissa formations carrying small round shields, the flanks covered by Thracian javelin cavalry and heavy cavalry, and for siege work torsion catapults, stone-throwers, siege towers and battering rams. The Seleucid rear was very deep: the Royal Road across Anatolia and the waterways of Mesopotamia could deliver troops, siege equipment and grain as far as the lower Orontes, and that was its greatest advantage in a war of endurance. The third parties have to be counted as well. The Gauls poured east from 279 BC and were defeated by Antiochus in Anatolia in 275 BC; that Gallic war pinned the Seleucid army in western Asia for a time, but it also freed the king's best troops to move south. Alongside them were the Phoenician city states and their local dynasts: the rulers of Tyre and Sidon each held their own ground, acting both as Ptolemaic agents in Syria and as internal allies of the Seleucids. Then there were the exiled nobles and mercenary captains of Anatolia and Asia Minor, courted by both sides. None of this war involved the general mobilisation of a people, neither state had the destruction of the other as its aim, and what was fought over was harbours, customs revenue and a border that could be held.
people: 兩位君主是全場的核心。托勒密二世·菲拉德爾福斯是這場戰爭的發動者：前二八三年他的父王托勒密一世去世，他清除母后與弟弟之後獨攬大權，隨即需要一場對外勝利來證明自己坐得住這個王位；他選了最近的目標——前二三〇年代以來始終沒有歸順的腓尼基沿岸。安條克一世·索提爾是塞琉古一世的兒子，前二八一年在安條克即位，此前已經在安納托利亞對高盧人打了三年苦戰，前二七五年以象兵與弓手在安納托利亞擊潰高盧大軍（戰場通常繫於呂卡翁一帶），從此得號索提爾，並把注意力從安納托利亞轉向南方。他的性格決定了本役的走向：他不肯把敘利亞拱手讓出，寧可把主力自安納托利亞調回，長期駐在奧龍特斯河一線；正是這道防線擋住了托勒密。腓尼基一端也有具名的人物：提爾與西頓的統治者是兩場圍城的對象，狄奧多羅斯記的提爾圍城裡寫到城中有主持抵抗的貴族與一整套備用的井水設施；塞琉古在敘利亞的內應則是那些不願接受托勒密駐軍與稅制的城邦派別。除此之外，戰場上真正發揮作用的是一批技術人員：築堤填海的土工、能操作扭力弩砲與投石機的技師，以及被兩方用重金互挖的傭兵將領；希臘化世界的工程兵與傭兵在這一時期已經成為常備軍的骨幹。史料方面，今人重建這場戰爭主要靠三份：狄奧多羅斯·西西里的《歷史文庫》第十九卷，記下提爾圍城最詳細的工程與攻城記載；波利比奧斯《史記》的殘篇，記下安條克與托勒密議和的經過；以及斯特拉波的《地理學》留下的腓尼基海岸與奧龍特斯河的地理與道路描述。古代編年只記年不記月，前線指揮官的姓名也大量失落，因此這場戰爭的戰術細節多靠結果反推。
peopleEn: Two monarchs stand at the centre of the story. Ptolemy II Philadelphus was the man who started the war: after his father Ptolemy I died in 283 BC he cleared out his mother and his brother and took sole power, and he then needed an external victory to prove that he could sit on the throne. He chose the nearest available target, the Phoenician coast, which since the 230s BC had never been fully brought to order. Antiochus I Soter, son of Seleucus I, had taken the throne at Antioch in 281 BC after three years of hard fighting against the Gauls in Anatolia; in 275 BC he broke the Gallic host with elephants and archers, the battlefield being usually placed in the Lycaonian region, won the name Soter, and turned his attention from Anatolia to the south. His temperament decided the shape of the campaign: he would not hand Syria over, and he moved the bulk of his army back from Anatolia to hold the line on the Orontes for the long term; it was that line that stopped Ptolemy. On the Phoenician side there are named figures as well: the rulers of Tyre and Sidon were the objects of the two sieges, and the account of the siege of Tyre preserved by Diodorus shows the city's aristocratic leadership and its full provision of wells; the Seleucid fifth column in Syria consisted of those city factions unwilling to accept a Ptolemaic garrison and tax regime. Beyond them, the men who actually decided things on the ground were technical specialists: the earthworkers who built the causeway, the engineers who served the torsion catapults and stone-throwers, and the mercenary officers whom both sides bought with gold, since engineers and mercenaries had by this period become a standing part of Hellenistic armies. The reconstruction of this war rests on three main sources: Book 19 of Diodorus Siculus' Bibliotheca Historica, which preserves the fullest account of the siege works at Tyre; the surviving fragments of Polybius, which carry the account of the settlement between Antiochus and Ptolemy; and Strabo's Geography, which preserves the geography and the road system of the Phoenician coast and the Orontes. The ancient chronicles give years but not months, and the names of most field commanders are lost, so much of the tactical detail has to be inferred backwards from the outcome.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛得先放對位置。它是公元前九百年前後成形的新亞述式樣：短木柄，長刃鐵矛頭，前端以套筒固定在柄上，柄尾常留一小段配重鐵箍；亞述人把它與弓、箭、斧頭捆成同一套步兵裝備，前排持矛與盾正面頂住，兩翼的弓箭手以箭雨覆蓋，再由雙輪輕戰車弓手與騎兵在兩翼機動。這種矛兵與弓兵混編、以投射火力先行的辦法，是近東步兵戰術的老譜。但到了前二七四年，它本身早已是出土物：亞述的尼尼微於前六一二年陷落，亞述王國在幾十年間瓦解，此後近東的長矛一路改成更長、更輕的薩里沙，配上小圓盾成為希臘化方陣的骨架。也就是說，卡面這件兵器在這場戰爭裡的位置是對照件與譜系標本——它標示出希臘化方陣所承襲的那一支技術傳統：把矛兵放在方陣中央、把弓手放在兩翼，而不是像後來羅馬人那樣先用標槍洗臉再進劍。當時真正上陣的裝備有兩套。塞琉古方面：薩里沙長矛配小圓盾（希臘化的方陣在亞洲化之後常見的盾型）、青銅或鐵盔、鱗甲與亞麻甲，近身用短劍與雙刃劍；投射方面用弓（塞琉古弓、克里特弓）、投石索、標槍，攻城則是扭力弩砲、投石機、攻城塔、撞錘與填土斜坡。埃及方面：馬其頓與希臘重裝方陣是野戰骨幹，埃及步兵與埃及弓手補上兵源，非洲象在攻城時用來撞門與壓制城頭投射位，埃及式亞麻鱗甲與圓盾常見於守城與守營的部隊。托勒密在提爾用的是工程手段：在海峽最窄處填土築堤，把島上的城與大陸接通，再用海軍封住南面的港口。運輸方面，埃及靠海運船隊沿腓尼基海岸配送糧秣與攻城器材，軍隊的馬匹、攻城塔與糧車靠陸路從安條克方向輸送，兩者的效率差距是這場戰爭勝負所在之一。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card has to be placed in position first. It is the type that took shape around 900 BC in the Neo-Assyrian army: a short wooden shaft carrying a long-bladed iron head, the head fixed to the shaft by a socket, with a short iron-shod butt-spike left at the lower end. The Assyrians bound it together with the bow, the arrow and the axe into a single infantry kit, with spear and shield in front, archers covering the ground with arrow-fall from the flanks, and light two-wheeled war chariots and cavalry manoeuvring on the wings. That mixture of spear troops and archers, with missile fire opening the action, is the old Near Eastern school of infantry warfare. By 274 BC, however, the weapon itself was an archaeological object: Nineveh fell in 612 BC and the Assyrian kingdom dissolved within a few decades, and the long spear of the Near East had since been replaced by the longer and lighter sarissa, carried with the small round shield to form the skeleton of the Hellenistic phalanx. The weapon on the card therefore stands in this war as a reference piece and a pedigree marker: it identifies the technical tradition the Hellenistic phalanx inherited, that of holding the spears in the centre of the formation and the archers on the wings, rather than the later Roman system of softening the enemy with javelins before the sword went in. The equipment actually in the line was of two kinds. The Seleucids used sarissas with small round shields, the common shield of the Asianised phalanx, bronze or iron helmets, scale and linen armour, and short swords and double-edged blades for close work; for missile work, bows (Seleucid, Cretan), slings and javelins; for siege, torsion catapults, stone-throwers, siege towers, battering rams and earthen ramps. The Egyptians used Macedonian and Greek heavy infantry as the backbone of the field army, with Egyptian foot and archers to supply the numbers, African elephants to smash gates and suppress the defenders' missile positions during sieges, and Egyptian linen scale armour and round shields common in garrisons and in the defence of camps. Against Tyre, Ptolemy relied on engineering: at the narrowest point of the strait he filled the sea with earth and rubble to build a causeway joining the island city to the mainland, and then closed the southern harbour with his fleet. In the matter of transport, Egypt fed the Phoenician front by sea, with grain and siege equipment carried along the coast, while horses, siege towers and baggage trains moved overland from the Antioch direction; the difference in efficiency between the two supply systems was itself one of the reasons the war went the way it did.
tactics: 這場戰爭的樣貌由攻城與野戰兩條線構成。托勒密的第一步是提爾：托勒密二世在腓尼基海岸用最老的辦法打最難的目標——海峽最窄處不足五百米，島上的城三面是海，他把土石填海築成一道連接島與大陸的堤道，把攻城塔、投石機與隊伍直接推上堤面，再用海軍封住南面的港口，切斷城內的漁獲與援兵；狄奧多羅斯記這場圍城歷時七個月，靠的是土方、封鎖與飢餓，而不是一次強攻。城內靠井水、外海的漁船與儲糧撐到最後，城市最終接受條件。托勒密接著取西頓，再把戰線推向奧龍特斯河，試圖直取塞琉古在敘利亞的核心。他的問題在於攻城分兵：埃及主力一旦離開港口，就靠馬車隊把海運轉成陸運維持，越往北走補給線越長，速度越慢。塞琉古的應法是守住河道與平原，不與托勒密在城邑上纏鬥，卻靠安納托利亞的皇家大道把援軍與攻城器材一批批送到，時間站在自己這邊。會戰的樣子仍是希臘化世界的標準打法：塞琉古以縱深方陣正面承托，兩翼由重裝騎兵與象兵掩護，把托勒密偏向海岸的方陣往西頓方向壓；托勒密在內陸會戰中沒有取勝，攻勢退回海岸。最後的收場不是決戰，而是外交：前二七一年左右兩國議和，托勒密保住腓尼基的港口，塞琉古守住奧龍特斯河谷與內陸。以工程、海運與時間換來的戰線，就這樣被一紙條約固定下來。
tacticsEn: The war divides into two lines, siege and field battle. Ptolemy's first move was Tyre, and he took on the oldest target in the Near East with the oldest method: the strait is less than five hundred metres wide at its narrowest, the city on the island has sea on three sides, and he built a causeway of earth and stone across the water to join the city to the mainland, ran his siege towers, stone-throwers and formations straight along the top of it, and at the same time closed the southern harbour with his fleet, cutting the city off from its fishing boats and from any relief; Diodorus records that the siege lasted seven months, and that it was won by earthworks, blockade and hunger rather than by a single assault. The city held out on its wells, on the fishing that still came in from outside and on stored grain, and in the end accepted terms. Ptolemy took Sidon next and pushed the line towards the Orontes, aiming straight at the Seleucid heart of Syria. His problem was that sieges divided his army: once the Egyptian main force left the coast it depended on baggage trains to convert sea transport into land supply, and the further north it went the longer and slower the line of supply became. The Seleucid answer was to hold the river and the plain, to avoid being drawn into a contest over towns, and to bring up reinforcements and siege material batch by batch along the Royal Road of Anatolia, so that time stood on the king's side. The field engagement followed the standard Hellenistic pattern: the Seleucids took the weight of the enemy in a deep phalanx, covered the wings with heavy cavalry and elephants, and pressed the coastal Ptolemaic formation back towards Sidon; Ptolemy gained nothing in the field inland, and the offensive was driven back to the coast. The war was not ended by a decisive battle but by diplomacy: around 271 BC the two kings made terms, Ptolemy kept the Phoenician harbours, and the Seleucids kept the Orontes valley and the interior. The line, bought with engineering, sea transport and time, was fixed in place by a treaty.
data: 可核對的數字不多，而且分散在幾處。時間上，這場戰爭一般繫於前二七四年到前二七一年，約三至四年；提爾的圍城歷時七個月。地理上，提爾是海島上的城，與本土之間的海峽最窄處不足五百米；提爾到西頓的直線距離約四十公里，兩城之間是腓尼基最密的葡萄園與紫染工坊地帶，也是托勒密在海陸兩側同時施壓的接點；亞歷山大港到提爾的直線距離約六百五十公里，越過地中海的航線更長，糧秣與攻城器材全靠這條海路；提爾到奧龍特斯河下游的都城安條克直線約三百公里，安條克是塞琉古的補給終點，也是它能把兵員源源送上來的原因。兵員方面，古代文獻沒有留下可信的點兵數字，可確認的只是量級：托勒密投入野戰的方陣兵與埃及步兵在數萬量級，攻城軍團、象隊與工匠另計；安條克一方能從安納托利亞調來的軍隊以萬計。裝備方面，馬其頓方陣的標準縱深是十六排，薩里沙長矛長約四至六公尺；托勒密王朝的常備象群常被估計在數百頭的規模，有說法給出接近八百頭的上限，但那是估算，不能當作實數。工程方面，堤道長度按海峽寬度推算，填方量以數十萬立方米計；圍城七個月意味著攻方要為數萬人的軍隊維持糧秣，軍需的重量遠大於攻城塔本身。結果方面，沒有留下可核實的陣亡數字，兩國也沒有在會戰中傾盡主力，史料對這場戰爭的記載本身就偏於攻城與條約，而不是殘殺。月份方面，古代編年只記年不記月，本卡所標的四月是依春季開戰的常例標記，並非文獻所載。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few and scattered. In time, the war is generally dated from 274 to 271 BC, about three to four years, and the siege of Tyre lasted seven months. In geography, Tyre was a city on an island, and the strait between it and the mainland is less than five hundred metres wide at its narrowest; the straight-line distance from Tyre to Sidon is about forty kilometres, and the ground between the two cities was the densest belt of Phoenician vineyards and purple-dye workshops, as well as the point at which Ptolemy could press on land and sea at once; the straight-line distance from Alexandria to Tyre is about six hundred and fifty kilometres, and the sea route across the Mediterranean is longer still, so grain and siege material came entirely by that sea lane; the straight-line distance from Tyre to Antioch on the lower Orontes is about three hundred kilometres, and Antioch was the end of the Seleucid supply line, the place from which troops could be fed forward without end. On strength, the ancient literature leaves no trustworthy count: the only thing that can be confirmed is the order of magnitude. The phalanx infantry and Egyptian foot that Ptolemy put into the field ran to tens of thousands, with the siege train, the elephants and the engineers counted separately, and the army Antiochus could bring down from Anatolia was measured in thousands of tens. On equipment, the standard depth of the Macedonian phalanx was sixteen ranks and the sarissa was roughly four to six metres long; the standing elephant herd of the Ptolemaic monarchy is usually estimated in the hundreds, with an upper figure near eight hundred, but that is an estimate and not a return. On engineering, the length of the causeway follows from the width of the strait, and the volume of fill runs to hundreds of thousands of cubic metres; a seven-month siege means that the besieger had to feed an army of tens of thousands, and the baggage weighed far more than the siege towers did. On results, no verifiable casualty figure survives: neither state was committed to destruction in the field battle, and the ancient record of this war is weighted towards the siege and the treaty rather than towards slaughter. As to months, the ancient chronicles give years and not months; the April entered on this card follows the usual convention of a spring opening and is not attested in the sources.
cause: 打起來有四層原因。最外層是繼承與分割：前三二三年亞歷山大死後的瓜分，把地中海東岸切成兩塊，前二八七年左右的三分阿拉卡德洛斯條約把基列敘利亞（奧龍特斯河谷與安條克一帶）連同腓尼基判給托勒密，把安納托利亞與兩河判給塞琉古；托勒密得到的是一條伸到埃及門口的邊界，塞琉古得到的卻是「亞洲」。第二層是安條克一世的收復計畫：他自前二八一年即位起就沒有能力收回敘利亞，前二七五年在安納托利亞擊敗高盧人後，終於騰出可用之兵，也需要一場勝利來把王位坐穩。第三層是托勒密二世的處境：前二八三年父王去世後，他清洗了王室，血統繼承尚未獲得臣民完全接受；腓尼基沿岸在他治下一直是半獨立的高稅收區，提爾與西頓的統治者與當地貴族對托勒密的駐軍與稅制不滿，這就給了塞琉古的內應以可乘之機。第四層是高盧人帶來的連鎖反應：高盧大軍在前二七九年至前二七五年橫掃希臘與安納托利亞，既逼出托勒密二世在敘利亞的應戰（據說他一度在奧龍特斯河上游擊退深入的高盧人），也讓安條克一世在東邊贏得可以南下的資本。於是本來只是邊界糾紛的一條河谷，變成了兩個王朝各自要拿來證明正統的戰爭。
causeEn: There are four layers of cause. The outermost is inheritance and partition: after Alexander's death in 323 BC the eastern Mediterranean was cut in two, and the Treaty of Triparadisus of about 287 BC gave Coele-Syria, the Orontes valley and Antioch, together with Phoenicia, to the Ptolemids, while Anatolia and the two riverlands went to the Seleucids. What Ptolemy received was a frontier running up to the gate of Egypt; what Seleucus received was Asia. The second layer is Antiochus I's plan of recovery: from his accession in 281 BC he had never had the means to take Syria back, and after beating the Gauls in Anatolia in 275 BC he finally had troops he could move and a victory that would steady his throne. The third layer is Ptolemy II's own position: after his father's death in 283 BC he had cleared the palace, and his blood claim to the throne had not yet been fully accepted; the Phoenician coast had remained under him a half-autonomous and heavily taxed region, and the rulers and notables of Tyre and Sidon were dissatisfied with his garrisons and his tax arrangements, which gave the Seleucid agents a way in. The fourth layer is the chain reaction set off by the Gauls: the Gallic host that swept through Greece and Anatolia between 279 and 275 BC forced Ptolemy II to fight in Syria, where he is said to have turned the Gauls back in the upper valley of the Orontes, and it gave Antiochus I the capital he needed to strike south. What began as a quarrel over a river valley thus turned into a war in which each of the two dynasties had to prove its own legitimacy.
impact: 這場戰爭留下的東西，比它的戰果更多。第一是邊界：前二七一年後的安排，把腓尼基海岸判給托勒密、把奧龍特斯河谷與基列敘利亞內陸留給塞琉古，兩國此後兩百年的五次敘利亞戰爭，幾乎每一次都在推移這條線——第二次敘利亞戰爭中安條克二世一度奪回提爾與西頓，前二五二年托勒密三世又在貝魯特之戰後攻入安條克，第四次與第五次再把邊界推到拉多底亞與帕努斯。托勒密王朝由此得到一個關鍵的海上立足點：以提爾與西頓為基地控制東地中海的商路，紫染、玻璃與黎巴嫩雪松的關稅，加上亞歷山大港的船隊，使埃及的財政在缺少亞洲領土的情況下仍然穩定，這是托勒密王朝能延續兩百年的基礎。塞琉古的教訓同樣清楚：把注意力壓在西邊，就要放棄安納托利亞的總督問題與東方的巴克特利亞；安條克一世在西邊止住了托勒密，也在東邊留下了真空。軍事技術上，這場戰爭留下兩份教材：提爾的填海築堤是希臘化世界最詳細的一次攻城工程記錄，後世研究亞歷山大本人於前三三二年圍攻提爾的工程，以及高盧人與阿該亞同盟的攻城手法，都以它為參照；北線的會戰則再次示範了象兵對方陣的作用與限度。第三是外交的示範：安條克一世此前娶了敘利亞王德米特里一世的女兒斯特拉托尼刻，這門婚姻在第一次敘利亞戰爭之後仍然是兩朝關係的軟肋，前二四六年斯特拉托尼刻在拉多底亞被殺，直接引爆第三次敘利亞戰爭——一場為港口與稅收而打的戰爭，最後把它的主角捲進了更長的王朝內鬥。
impactEn: What this war left behind is greater than what it won. First, the border: after the settlement of about 271 BC, Phoenicia went to the Ptolemids and the Orontes valley and inland Coele-Syria stayed with the Seleucids, and of the five Syrian Wars fought over the next two centuries almost every one shifted that line. In the Second Syrian War Antiochus II took Tyre and Sidon back for a time, and in about 252 BC Ptolemy III broke through at the battle of Berytus and entered Antioch; the Fourth and the Fifth pushed the line out to Raphia and Panus. The Ptolemaic dynasty thereby gained a decisive foothold on the sea: with Tyre and Sidon as bases it controlled the trade routes of the eastern Mediterranean, and the customs on Tyrian purple, glass and Lebanese cedar, together with the fleet of Alexandria, kept the finances of Egypt stable even after the loss of the Asian territories, and that is the foundation on which the Ptolemaic house stood for two more centuries. The lesson for the Seleucids was equally plain: to press the campaign in the west was to abandon the problem of the satraps in Anatolia and the new kingdom of Bactria in the east. Antiochus I stopped Ptolemy in the west, and in the east he left a vacuum. On military technique the war left two textbooks. The causeway at Tyre is the most detailed surviving record of Hellenistic siege engineering, and the study of Alexander's own siege of Tyre in 332 BC, and of the sieges of the Gauls and of the Achaean League, all take it as a reference; the campaign in the north, for its part, demonstrated once more the effect and the limits of elephants against a phalanx. Third, there was a lesson in diplomacy. Antiochus I had married Stratonice, the daughter of the king of Syria Demetrius I, and that marriage remained the soft spot in the relations of the two houses after the First Syrian War; in 246 BC Stratonice was killed at Raphia, and that murder triggered the Third Syrian War. A war fought for harbours and customs revenue ended by pulling its own protagonists into a longer dynastic quarrel.
result: 前二七一年前後，托勒密二世與安條克一世議和：托勒密保住提爾與西頓等腓尼基港市，塞琉古保住奧龍特斯河谷與基列敘利亞內陸，沒有決戰，沒有滅國，兩國在邊界上各退一步。戰役層面的帳要這樣算：托勒密發動戰爭，用七個月的堤道圍城拿下提爾、以閃擊取西頓，戰術上得一；但他率主力深入敘利亞後，被安條克以方陣正面與象騎兩翼反擊壓回海岸，攻勢終止於河谷北側，未能占領安條克與奧龍特斯河下游的內陸據點；安條克付出的是把安納托利亞精兵調離的代價，遠征線拉長，但他的軍隊始終在本土補給範圍之內，時間站在國王這邊。雙方都沒有在會戰中傾盡主力，因此這場戰爭的損失主要消耗在攻城、行軍與斷糧，而不是一次決定性的殘殺，史料也沒有留下可核實的陣亡數字。長期看，這個結局是全場最耐嚼的部分：第一次敘利亞戰爭沒有解決任何東西，它只是把「敘利亞歸誰」變成一條所有人都記住的線。前二六一年安條克一世被高盧傭兵刺殺，繼承者安條克二世在第二次敘利亞戰爭中把提爾與西頓重新拿下，前二五二年托勒密三世才在貝魯特之戰後攻入安條克；直到前二〇〇年的帕努斯之戰與此後羅馬的介入，這條線才被徹底改寫。而托勒密二世在提爾得到的堤道與港口，則在他死後仍為埃及的東地中海航線服務了半個多世紀。
resultEn: Around 271 BC Ptolemy II and Antiochus I came to terms: Ptolemy kept the Phoenician ports of Tyre and Sidon, the Seleucids kept the Orontes valley and inland Coele-Syria, and there was no decisive battle and no destruction of a state; each gave ground on the line. The ledger of the campaign reads like this. Ptolemy began the war, took Tyre with a seven-month causeway siege, and carried Sidon by surprise, and in tactical terms he gained. But once he led his main force deep into Syria, Antiochus met him with a phalanx in front and elephants and cavalry on the wings, pressed him back towards the coast, and the offensive stopped north of the river valley without the capture of Antioch or the inland bases on the lower Orontes. Antiochus paid for it by moving the picked troops of Anatolia away, lengthening his lines of march, but his army remained inside the range of supply from home, and so time stood with the king. Neither side committed its main force to destruction, so the losses of this war were consumed mostly in siege, marching and hunger rather than in one annihilating battle, and the sources preserve no verifiable casualty figures. In the long run this outcome is the most instructive part of the whole business: the First Syrian War settled nothing; it only turned the question of who owned Syria into a line that everybody remembered. In 261 BC Antiochus I was killed by a Gallic mercenary, his successor Antiochus II took Tyre and Sidon back in the Second Syrian War, and it was not until the battle of Panus in 200 BC and the arrival of Rome that the line was rewritten for good. The causeway and the harbour that Ptolemy II won at Tyre, for their part, served Egypt's eastern Mediterranean routes for more than half a century after his death.
